references.text: God commands Noah to leave the ark with his family and all the animals – the direct reason why Noah obeys and goes out in verse 18.

God establishes His covenant with Noah before the flood, promising that Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives will enter the ark – a covenant fulfilled by their survival and exit from the ark.
Noah and his family enter the ark to be saved from the floodwaters, which mirrors their departure from the ark after the waters had receded.
Describes Noah, Shem, Ham, Japheth, Noah's wife, and the three daughters-in-law entering the ark – exactly the same list of people as in the exit account in 8:18.
After Noah and his family leave the ark, God blesses them and gives them instructions, marking the beginning of their new life after the flood.
Noah's faith is highlighted as an example – by faith he built the ark and saved his family, encompassing the entire sequence of events from entering to leaving the ark.
Peter refers to Noah as the eighth person preserved through the flood, confirming that Noah and his family of eight people were saved.
Highlights the continuity in Noah's obedience: he did everything God commanded, both in building the ark and in going out of it.
Explains the theological consequence of the departure: the three sons who went out became the whole of humanity.
Connects the departure directly to the subsequent scattering of nations across the earth.
Confirms the identity of those who left the ark and sets the stage for the following genealogies.
Explains the theological reason why Noah and his household were saved: his righteousness and walking with God.
